summary: Modern databases and data platforms have rapidly embedded native AI and ML capabilities, eliminating the need to move data to external systems for inference, embedding generation, and vector search. By 2026, vector database adoption has grown 377% year over year, with 75% of enterprise AI applications expected to depend on vector search, driving platforms like Snowflake, BigQuery, and PostgreSQL to integrate LLM functions, embedding pipelines, and similarity search directly into their query engines. The competitive landscape now spans purpose-built vector databases and general-purpose platforms, with pgvector on PostgreSQL emerging as the lowest-friction path for teams already on Postgres infrastructure.

databases.name: Snowflake
databases.description: Snowflake Cortex AI is a suite of fully managed ML and LLM functions built directly into the Snowflake AI Data Cloud. It provides text-to-SQL generation, embedding creation, sentiment analysis, summarization, classification, and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) pipelines without moving data outside Snowflake. With the general availability of Snowflake Postgres (announced February 2026), Cortex AI now integrates natively with Postgres workloads running inside Snowflake, enabling embedding generation and text-to-SQL on Postgres tables via pgvector. Cortex Search and Cortex Analyst extend these capabilities into semantic search and natural language querying over structured data.
databases.llm_integration: Native LLM functions via Cortex AI including COMPLETE, EMBED_TEXT, SUMMARIZE, SENTIMENT, and CLASSIFY using hosted models such as Mistral, LLaMA, and Snowflake Arctic. Integrates with Snowflake Postgres and pgvector for vector similarity search. Supports Cortex Search for hybrid keyword and semantic retrieval.
databases.pricing_notes: Cortex AI functions are billed in Snowflake credits. Embedding and LLM inference consume credits per token processed, which vary by model size and type. Snowflake Postgres is priced separately with compute and storage costs layered on top of Cortex usage. Enterprise contracts typically bundle credits; on-demand rates apply for pay-as-you-go accounts.

databases.name: Google BigQuery
databases.description: BigQuery ML allows data teams to create and execute machine learning models using standard SQL inside BigQuery, supporting logistic regression, boosted trees, matrix factorization, time series forecasting, and deep neural networks. BigQuery integrates directly with Vertex AI, enabling users to call hosted foundation models and custom Vertex AI endpoints from SQL queries using the ML.GENERATE_TEXT and ML.EMBED_TEXT functions. Vector search is supported natively through BigQuery Vector Search, which uses approximate nearest neighbor algorithms to query embedding columns stored in BigQuery tables at scale.
databases.llm_integration: ML.GENERATE_TEXT and ML.EMBED_TEXT functions connect BigQuery directly to Vertex AI hosted models including Gemini 1.5 Pro, Gemini Flash, and text-embedding models. Remote model connections allow SQL-based inference against any Vertex AI endpoint. Supports grounding, RAG pipelines, and multimodal embeddings through Vertex AI integration.
databases.pricing_notes: BigQuery ML model training and inference are billed per byte processed for SQL-based models. LLM inference via ML.GENERATE_TEXT is billed based on Vertex AI token pricing for the underlying model, passed through at Google Cloud rates. BigQuery Vector Search queries are charged at standard BigQuery compute rates. Enterprise pricing available through Google Cloud committed use contracts.

databases.name: PostgreSQL
databases.description: pgvector is an open-source PostgreSQL extension that adds vector similarity search capabilities directly to any Postgres instance, supporting exact and approximate nearest neighbor search using HNSW and IVFFlat indexes. It stores embedding vectors as native column types and queries them using SQL, making it the lowest-friction path to vector search for teams already running Postgres. pgai is a complementary extension developed by Timescale that adds LLM inference, embedding generation, and chunking functions callable from SQL, enabling full AI pipelines without leaving the database. Snowflake Postgres now supports pgvector natively as of 2026, and it integrates with platforms like Databricks and Supabase.
databases.llm_integration: pgai connects PostgreSQL to external LLM providers including OpenAI, Ollama, and Anthropic via SQL functions, allowing embedding generation and text completion queries to run inside Postgres transactions. pgvector handles the storage and retrieval layer while pgai handles the model inference layer. Supabase Vector and Timescale Cloud offer managed hosted environments with both extensions pre-installed.
databases.pricing_notes: pgvector and pgai are fully open-source and free to self-host on any Postgres instance. Managed offerings such as Supabase Vector, Timescale Cloud, and Neon include pgvector in their standard plans with pricing based on compute and storage tiers. LLM inference through pgai is billed by the upstream provider such as OpenAI at their standard API rates. Snowflake Postgres with pgvector is billed under Snowflake compute and storage pricing.

databases.name: Amazon Aurora + Redshift
databases.description: Aurora ML enables Aurora MySQL and Aurora PostgreSQL databases to call Amazon SageMaker and Amazon Bedrock models directly from SQL queries using a built-in ml_predict function, supporting inference on row-level data without ETL pipelines. Aurora PostgreSQL also supports pgvector, enabling vector similarity search on embedding data stored in Aurora tables. Redshift ML allows data warehouse users to create, train, and invoke machine learning models using SQL via integration with Amazon SageMaker AutoPilot, and Redshift supports vector similarity functions for semantic search workloads. Amazon Bedrock integration across both services enables access to foundation models including Claude, Llama, and Titan from within SQL workflows.
databases.llm_integration: Aurora ML integrates with Amazon Bedrock to call foundation models such as Anthropic Claude, Amazon Titan, and Meta Llama directly from SQL using the aws_bedrock extension. Aurora PostgreSQL with pgvector supports embedding storage and nearest neighbor retrieval. Redshift ML uses SageMaker AutoPilot for model training and supports PREDICT functions for batch and real-time inference from within Redshift queries.
databases.pricing_notes: Aurora ML inference calls are billed per request to the underlying SageMaker or Bedrock endpoint at standard AWS rates. Aurora PostgreSQL with pgvector is included at no additional cost for the extension; compute and storage are billed at standard Aurora instance pricing. Redshift ML training jobs are billed through SageMaker compute costs; inference predictions are billed per query at Redshift compute rates. Bedrock model calls are charged per input and output token by model.

databases.name: Databricks
databases.description: Databricks provides an end-to-end AI and ML platform built on top of the Lakehouse architecture, combining MLflow for experiment tracking, model registry, and deployment with Mosaic AI for building, fine-tuning, and serving large language models. DBRX is Databricks' own open-source foundation model optimized for enterprise use cases and deployable within a customer's own cloud environment. Databricks Vector Search is a managed vector database integrated into the platform that indexes Delta Lake tables and serves approximate nearest neighbor queries for RAG and semantic search workloads. The platform integrates with pgvector-compatible workflows and supports data mirroring from Snowflake Postgres.
databases.llm_integration: Mosaic AI Model Serving supports deployment of DBRX, Llama, Mistral, and custom fine-tuned models with REST API endpoints. MLflow tracks experiments, manages model versions, and integrates with LangChain and LlamaIndex for RAG pipeline orchestration. Databricks Vector Search indexes embeddings from Delta Lake tables and serves queries via SDK and REST, with embedding generation handled by Foundation Model APIs or external providers.
databases.pricing_notes: Databricks billing is based on Databricks Units (DBUs) consumed by compute clusters and SQL warehouses. MLflow is open-source and free; managed MLflow on Databricks is included in platform tiers. Mosaic AI Model Serving is billed per DBU based on model size and throughput. Databricks Vector Search is charged based on indexed data volume and query load. Enterprise pricing is available through AWS, Azure, and GCP marketplace agreements.

databases.name: MongoDB Atlas
databases.description: MongoDB Atlas Vector Search is a fully managed vector search capability built into Atlas that allows developers to store embedding vectors alongside their operational document data and query them using approximate nearest neighbor search with HNSW indexing. It supports hybrid search combining vector similarity with full-text and metadata filters in a single aggregation pipeline query, making it suitable for RAG applications, semantic search, and recommendation systems. Atlas integrates with major embedding providers and LLM frameworks including LangChain, LlamaIndex, and Hugging Face, and supports pre-filtering on document fields to narrow vector search scope before similarity ranking.
databases.llm_integration: Atlas Vector Search integrates with OpenAI, Cohere, Hugging Face, and Amazon Bedrock for embedding generation, and connects to LangChain and LlamaIndex as a vector store backend for RAG pipelines. Atlas Charts and the Aggregation Framework allow vector search results to feed downstream analytics. MongoDB Atlas also supports triggers and functions that can call external LLM APIs as part of automated data processing workflows.
databases.pricing_notes: Atlas Vector Search is available on M10 dedicated clusters and above; it is not available on the free M0 tier or shared clusters. Pricing is based on Atlas cluster size with vector search indexes consuming additional storage billed per GB. Higher cluster tiers unlock higher index limits and query throughput. Serverless Atlas instances have limited vector search support. Enterprise and committed use pricing is available through MongoDB sales.
